title: Operate Vizier workflows and installation
summary: Initialize or diagnose Vizier, inspect and recover exact runs and attempts, cancel active work, or deploy the current-user binary and Chancery selector without silently creating implementation work.
use_when: A Vizier ledger should be initialized or its storage and Nucleus readiness diagnosed.
An exact run or attempt should be listed, inspected, waited on, resumed, cancelled, or explicitly retried under its durable guards.
An authorized tested Vizier candidate should be installed through the selector-only current-user deployment.
do_not_use_when: A new implementation should be delegated; use vizier.implementation.delegate.
The desired effect is to edit a run's frozen documents, apply its candidate, move a caller branch, push, release, deploy another product, or delete retained state.
A failed or lost attempt lacks positive evidence that a successor is safe.
outcome: An explicitly initialized healthy ledger, an exact observed or safely advanced workflow state, a recorded cancellation or eligible successor attempt, or one coherent current-user Vizier binary and provider installation.
effects: Init creates or idempotently accepts the selected supported private ledger; doctor checks storage and strict Nucleus readiness without submitting implementation work.

List, show, status, and attempt show are body-free observations; document show explicitly reads one retained document; wait or resume may service durable nonterminal work; cancel records intent and asks Nucleus to cancel correlated jobs; attempt retry creates one explicit successor only when allowed.

The selector-only deployer stages a content-addressed release and changes the Vizier command and providers/vizier selectors together, but never initializes the ledger, calls Nucleus, runs a canary, or installs a daemon or schedule.
authority: Vizier's ledger owns run and attempt state, retry eligibility, cancellation intent, candidate identity, and domain success; Nucleus owns correlated runtime evidence and cancellation processing.
The operator owns authority to resume, cancel, retry, deploy, roll back, or remove an installation and must inspect exact current state first.
The Vizier deployer owns only Vizier content-addressed releases, its command selector, and its providers/vizier selector.
success: Every command reports the exact selected ledger, run, attempt, or installation result without following a replacement identity.
Recovery reuses persisted inputs and committed tool results; an explicit successor receives a new attempt and job identity only after safe terminal evidence.
Deployment proves matching binary/provider version, validates the complete provider bundle, and publishes or restores both owned selectors coherently.
failure_and_recovery: After uncertain operation, inspect the exact run and attempt before using wait, resume, or retry; never reconstruct success from final prose.

Cancellation cannot undo committed documents or worktree mutations. Unsafe workspaces, ambiguous Nucleus state, or exhausted remediation remain needs-attention; needs-attention wait and resume return the durable result without creating work, and retry is limited to the current resultless leaf.
A failed selector-only deployment restores the prior coherent selectors or detaches Vizier's public selectors fail-closed; rollback requires ledger compatibility and never authorizes state deletion.
privacy: The ledger, worktrees, Git objects, and Nucleus history may contain private implementation material and are retained separately from release bytes.
Diagnosis and deployment must not print, package, delete, or copy private document bodies, repository contents, Nucleus credentials, or tool payloads.
steps: Select the exact ledger and inspect doctor, run, attempt, and correlated Nucleus evidence before choosing an effect.
Use wait or resume for recoverable persisted work, cancel only with explicit authority, and retry only after positive eligibility evidence.
For deployment, validate a green absolute candidate and provider, capture the expected current selector, run the product deployer, then initialize state separately if intended.
checkpoints: The operation selects an exact run or attempt and does not alter frozen Markdown or source basis.
No recovery path creates an automatic retry, direct Codex invocation, or self-review exception.
Deployment changes only Vizier release and selector state and leaves the ledger, repositories, Nucleus, and services untouched.
adaptation: Use --database only for an intentional exact ledger boundary and --json for machine-readable evidence.
Prefer run wait for observation and mailbox service; use run resume after coordinator interruption; use attempt retry only for an eligible explicit successor.
Use --expected-current absent|releases/HASH to bind deployment to an observed selector when coordinating concurrent work.
stop_when: Ledger identity or integrity, Nucleus readiness, attempt terminality, workspace safety, or retry authority cannot be established.
Candidate version, provider bundle, release identity, selector ownership, or coherent rollback cannot be proved.
The requested effect would apply, push, release, deploy another product, edit requirements, or delete retained state.

interfaces.label: List or inspect runs
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/vizier [--database ABS] [--json] run list | run show RUN_ID | run status RUN_ID

interfaces.label: Wait, resume, or cancel
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/vizier [--database ABS] [--json] run wait RUN_ID | run resume RUN_ID | run cancel RUN_ID

interfaces.label: Inspect or retry attempt
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/vizier [--database ABS] [--json] attempt show ATTEMPT_ID | attempt retry ATTEMPT_ID

does_not_authorize: Creating a new run, changing frozen inputs, accepting edits, applying a candidate, or converting model/runtime evidence into domain success.
Running release.sh, pushing, deploying another product, restarting Nucleus, operating Semantics or Pratica, or deleting retained state.
Retrying ambiguous or active work, editing SQLite or Git references manually, or adopting foreign selectors.

consumers.statement: A current-user operator may initialize or diagnose Vizier, inspect and explicitly recover exact workflow records, or deploy the user-owned installation.

preconditions.statement: Workflow operations select one exact supported private ledger and exact run or attempt; effects require explicit authority and durable eligibility evidence.
Deployment requires a green regular absolute candidate binary, version-matched provider, absent or Vizier-owned selectors, and an unchanged observed or supplied expected-current selection.

inputs.statement: Inputs are an optional absolute ledger path, exact run or attempt identity, machine-output selection, and for deployment an absolute binary plus optional optimistic current selector.
Edited ledger rows, mutable document replacements, arbitrary process IDs, foreign selectors, implicit retry content, and destructive cleanup are unsupported.

outputs.statement: Outputs are exact initialization and readiness evidence, run and attempt state, one guarded recovery transition, or one coherent content-addressed command/provider installation; document show emits exact retained Markdown by default and supported metadata plus exact Markdown with --json, while unknown IDs fail without state change.

data_semantics.statement: Show and status are observations; wait may observe and service persisted work; resume continues the frozen run; cancel is durable intent plus individual runtime requests; retry is a new explicit attempt, never replayed success.
A terminal Nucleus state remains runtime evidence; only the corresponding committed Vizier records determine stage and run success.

identity_and_units.statement: Ledger path selects one workflow authority; run and attempt IDs select immutable lineage; Nucleus job ID selects one exact request; release SHA-256 selects installed bytes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspection reports current committed state at invocation, and explicit identities prevent following a replacement run or attempt; deployment rechecks current under product and catalog locks.
Doctor does not prove future Nucleus availability, status does not prove process liveness beyond recorded evidence, and deployment does not prove a real delegation run.

access.statement: Operations use current-user local filesystem and shell authority over the selected Vizier ledger, owned worktrees and installation paths, and the typed local Nucleus boundary.
Direct SQLite or Nucleus-state access, credential access, remote operation, foreign-selector takeover, and direct Codex execution are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Initialization is idempotent for supported state; recovery preserves exact requests and idempotent tool results; retry requires positive terminal evidence, the current resultless leaf, and a new identity; interrupted multi-round remediation resumes from the latest durable revision; cancellation does not erase history.
Deployment stages immutable bytes, serializes product and catalog publication, switches command and provider together, and restores both or detaches fail-closed before returning failure.

operational_limits.statement: Vizier has one selected ledger per invocation, no daemon or schedule, no automatic terminal retry, and a selector-only deployer that performs no database or workflow operation.
No recovery, cancellation, deployment, Nucleus, or workflow completion time and no retained-release or state-size bound is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Operation contract version 1 preserves exact-run operation, guarded successor retries, selector-only deployment, matching binary/provider release, and Nucleus execution contract 2 compatibility.
No universal support or migration window for older ledgers, releases, Git versions, macOS behavior, or Nucleus versions is promised.

reliances.statement: Doctor, wait, resume, cancellation, and retry evidence rely on Nucleus's typed execution operation while Vizier retains recovery and retry authority.
Workflow inspection and recovery rely on Git for retained object and worktree behavior, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that boundary.
